cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic cosine of 1
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0. Independently verified: cosh(0) = 1, so acosh(1) = 0 exactly (math.acosh(1) = 0.0)

cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic cosine of 10
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 2.9932228. Independently verified in Python: math.acosh(10) = 2.993222846126381 = ln(10 + sqrt(99)) -> 2.9932228 at 7 dp

cases.description: An argument below 1 is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that number must be "any real number equal to or greater than 1"; below that the inverse hyperbolic cosine is not real, which is Excel's documented #NUM! case
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the ACOT page states it explicitly for this function family
